This record was repaired after the fact: it cited the pre-squash branch tip, which the squash merge of PR #44 orphaned. The commit no longer exists in any clone, so the handoff conformance guard failed in CI while passing locally, where the orphaned object was still reachable. The range now names the squashed commit on main. This will recur for every package merged by squash and needs a protocol fix, not another repair.

Moving base_revision forward to the branch point drops the commits between the old base and that point. After a normal merge they remain in main's history and in the earlier increment's own handoff; after a SQUASH merge the individual commits are gone and that earlier handoff is the only surviving record of them. This is why the refresher rewrites only the handoff of the branch it is run on and never regenerates one whose branch has been merged.

If part of a branch is merged into main while work on it continues, the branch point moves onto the branch and the recomputed range describes LESS than the branch did. Nothing detects that: the drift check looks past the cited head, never before the cited base. A range narrower than the pull request should be read as this case.

npm run check:handoff now reports a stale base, but it is not in the npm run check chain, so a handoff hand-edited to a stale base and a matching file list still passes CI. See evidence/WP-0A-CON-008/handoff-base-revision.md.
